screens.question: Go pounds to dollars to euros to pounds. What is your profit, in pounds?

hints.text: Multiply the three rates.

explain.text: $1{,}000 \times 1.25 = 1{,}250$ dollars, then 1,150 euros, then £1,012. The product of the rates is 1.012, above 1. Any loop whose rates multiply above 1 is an arbitrage.

screens.title: What makes an arbitrage
screens.prose:
An arbitrage is a set of trades whose payoffs cancel on every outcome, with money left over. On a board with odds $o_i$ to 1 on exclusive outcomes, it exists when
$$\sum_i \frac{1}{o_i + 1} < 1.$$
The size is capped by the depth at each price.
screens.question: Odds of evens, 3 to 1 and 4 to 1. Staking £10, £5 and £4, what is locked?

hints.text: Each stake returns £20.
The stakes total $10 + 5 + 4 = 19$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. £20 comes back on £19 staked.

byKey.ret: That is the return, not the profit.

explain.text: $1/2 + 1/4 + 1/5 = 19/20$, so £19 locks £20. The profit is 1/20 of the payout. Arbitrage profits are small and depend on size.

widget.solution:
from fractions import Fraction


def cross_arb(asks, bids):
    """asks of one dealer, bids of another, each a list of
    (price, size) sorted best first. Match the cheapest ask
    with the highest bid while ask < bid.
    Return (units, profit)."""
    a = [list(x) for x in asks]
    b = [list(x) for x in bids]
    i = j = 0
    units, profit = 0, 0
    while i < len(a) and j < len(b) and a[i][0] < b[j][0]:
        q = min(a[i][1], b[j][1])
        units += q
        profit += q * (b[j][0] - a[i][0])
        a[i][1] -= q
        b[j][1] -= q
        if a[i][1] == 0:
            i += 1
        if b[j][1] == 0:
            j += 1
    return units, profit


def book_arb(odds):
    """odds: list of o for o-to-1 bets on exclusive outcomes.
    Return (stakes, profit) per £1 of payout as Fractions,
    or ([], Fraction(0)) if there is no arbitrage."""
    stakes = [Fraction(1, o + 1) for o in odds]
    profit = 1 - sum(stakes)
    if profit <= 0:
        return [], Fraction(0)
    return stakes, profit
widget.how: Check runs 8 hidden tests. `book_arb` must return exact Fractions; a board whose implied chances sum to 1 or more has no arbitrage.

In `book_arb`, the stake for $o$ to 1 is `Fraction(1, o + 1)`; the profit is 1 less their sum.

explain.text: Each unit locks £0.04 after costs, so 20,000 units lock £800. Gaps like this close in milliseconds, because machines watch both prices. In an interview you find them by hand, fast.

ideas: An arbitrage is a set of trades whose payoffs cancel on every outcome, with money left over.
Size it by the depth: match the best offer with the best bid while the offer is below the bid.
On a board, implied chances totalling below 1 lock a profit. Exactly 1 is fair; above 1 is the margin.
